goal: Build the per-child Solicitation send worker: the Dispatch gate, the unsubscribe token mint, the Messaging adapter call, and the terminal transaction that CASes the Outreach row, terminalizes the Lazy child, emits solicitation_sent, completes the outbox row and calls closeBatchIfSettled.
non_goals: No release poller, no drip pacing, no veto-window predicate, no expiry closure (all #900)
No cap decisions of any kind (amendment B3 — send workers never make cap decisions)
No release-level gates (Send breaker, platform ceiling, account cap, subscriptionGrantsFullAccess per B14) — all #900
No Judge logic; #900 owns the downgrade/hold split
No unknown sweep (D12d) — that is the releaser's backstop, #900
No auto-approval lane (#631), no review_attributed (#632), no staging flip (#633)
No migration — #898's migration 110 carries this family's schema work
No enqueueSolicitationSend typed helper — it ships with its producer in #900 (amendment B10)
No per-send rate-limit governor — Resend's per-team 10 req/s pacing is release-level, owned by #900
No change to src/lib/messaging/** — the Messaging adapter seam is complete and already carries the provider idempotency key
user_visible_behavior: A released Outreach row is dispatched through getMessagingAdapter() and reaches a real recipient as an email
The sent message carries a working per-ask one-click unsubscribe URL whose raw token exists only in memory and in the message
A recipient on the Suppression ledger is never contacted; the Outreach row goes withheld/suppressed and a solicitation_suppressed_at_dispatch analytics event is emitted
A contact whose location has no Attested postal address, or whose stored footer no longer byte-matches, is never contacted; the row goes withheld/no_postal_address or withheld/postal_address_mismatch
A message whose stored bytes fail the current ASK_LINT_VERSION or fail re-moderation is never sent; the row goes withheld/lint_failed or withheld/moderation_high
Turning SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED off stops further sends immediately; in-flight queued rows are left queued and cancelled later by #900's send_window_elapsed halt
A hard bounce terminalizes the Outreach row failed/send_failed with bounced_at stamped and zero retries
The Requests panel's batch closes on its own once the last Outreach row terminalizes, because every terminal writer calls closeBatchIfSettled in its own transaction
invariants: Invariant #2 transactional outbox: the terminal transaction completes its own outbox row in the SAME transaction as the state change; if it does not commit, the watchdog still owns the work (D12a)
Invariant #5 approval tokens never stored raw: only the SHA-256 hash of the unsubscribe token reaches Postgres; the raw token exists in memory and in the sent message only
Invariant #10 Node.js native crypto: node:crypto for the hash and the UUIDv7 id, never crypto-js
Invariant #12 entry points orchestrate: worker/jobs/solicitation-send.ts parses and delegates; retry classification lives in its own named module with focused tests
Invariant #15 explicit DB client: src/lib/solicitation/** takes sql / tx as a parameter and never imports @/lib/db/server
Never hold a Postgres lock across a slow remote call: re-lint and re-moderation run before tx1 opens; the provider call runs with no lock held
At-least-once outbox delivery must never mean at-least-once email: every provider call carries the outreach row id as its idempotency key (D12b)
provider_message_id is persisted on every successful send — it is the only join key the Solicitation lane can attribute a bounce or complaint on
solicitation_sent is emitted on the Lazy child with unit_count = 1, never on the Send batch parent
closeBatchIfSettled has one owner and is called in the same transaction as every terminalization
The byte-for-byte Owner approval contract is over the STORED bytes; unsubscribe-URL and review-link placeholder substitution is excluded, and the postal address is part of the byte-match
The Dispatch gate is per-CHILD and therefore per-CONTACT; no account-level fact is evaluated here
solicitation_outreach.moderation_status / moderation_detail stay render provenance (amendment B1) and are never overwritten by the dispatch verdict
edge_cases: A retry finds the Outreach row already in sending: resume — skip the Dispatch gate, re-issue the provider call with the same idempotency key, then run tx2. Re-gating could record withheld for a message that already reached a real person (the D12d lie-with-teeth argument).

SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED flips off between release and dispatch: defer — leave the row queued, complete the outbox row, record a spine step, do not send and do not throw. 091/110 have no flag_off withheld reason, so the row must not be terminalized here.
The batch is halted before the child runs: the halt sweep already cancelled rendered/queued rows, so the child finds delivery_status='cancelled', no-ops and completes its outbox row normally.
OPENAI_MODERATION_ENABLED is false: a clean provider verdict is a DISPATCH precondition (#623 §3.4), so this is treated identically to a provider error and the child is never sent.
A dispatch retry after the token insert: the mint is idempotent on outreach_id, so the retry re-uses the existing token row and the substituted body is byte-stable.
Provider 4xx invalid-recipient / hard bounce: terminal, zero retries, failed + send_failed + bounced_at, feeding the Suppression ledger.
Provider 5xx, timeout or rate limit (including a Resend per-team 429): retryable under standard max_attempts with BullMQ's bounded jittered backoff.
Retry exhaustion: the colocated 'failed' hook writes failed / send_exhausted and calls closeBatchIfSettled, so a dead child still settles its batch.
Two concurrent terminal writers on the same batch: closeBatchIfSettled CASes send_closed_at on NULL, so the second writes nothing.
A gate withhold still counts as a dispatch attempt: the Lazy child is created, its steps are recorded, and it terminalizes in the same transaction with no solicitation_sent outcome.

rollback_plan: No migration, so rollback is a flag flip plus a revert. SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is off in every environment and stays off through this merge; with it off the worker registers and no-ops, so the merge is inert. To back out after a flip: set SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED=false on Railway (via the flag-flip skill), which stops further dispatch immediately; in-flight queued rows are cancelled by #900's send_window_elapsed halt at the 72h boundary. Code rollback is a plain revert of the PR — no schema state to unwind.
observability: A structured worker log line per dispatch from createWorkerLogger('solicitation-send', correlationId) carrying outreachId, gate verdict and disposition_reason — never the message body, subject, recipient or raw token
A solicitation_suppressed_at_dispatch analytics event whenever the suppression item withholds a send (already registered by migration 097 and src/lib/analytics/events.ts)
agent_run_steps rows for the gate verdict and the send result on the Lazy child, and a solicitation_sent outcome row per successful send — the value ledger that proves sends happened
solicitation_outreach.provider_message_id populated on every sent row — its absence on a sent row is the signal that bounce attribution is broken

attachJobFailureSink raises a real Sentry issue on the terminal attempt; the colocated failed hook writes failed / send_exhausted so an exhausted child is visible in the domain table as well as in Sentry

How I would know it broke: sent rows with NULL provider_message_id, Outreach rows stuck in sending past the grace period, or a solicitation_sent count that does not match the sent-row count for a batch
